title: NY State Assembly · District 76
area: Manhattan's Upper East Side, Yorkville and Roosevelt Island.

context.text: Both the Democratic and Republican primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled. Incumbent Rebecca Seawright (D/WFP) advanced unopposed; Louis Puliafito (R), who has run against Seawright in multiple prior elections, also advanced unopposed after Mike Zumbluskas withdrew from the Republican primary.

summary.text: Rebecca Seawright is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent seeking re-election to a seventh term. She chairs the Assembly Aging Committee and sits on Ways and Means, Codes, Higher Education and Judiciary; her legislative focus has centered on aging, disability rights, education funding and the state Equal Rights Amendment.

background.text: First woman elected to represent the 76th Assembly District, first elected in 2014.
Serves as a Director of the Legislative Women's Caucus and participates in the Bipartisan Pro-Choice, Jewish, Environmental and Gun Reform legislative caucuses.
Previously chaired the People with Disabilities Committee, the Majority Steering Committee, and the Task Force on Women's Issues, and served as Secretary of the Majority Conference.

priorities.text: Aging and disability rights: chairs the Aging Committee and advocates for direct support professionals, including as lead sponsor of legislation to establish a direct-support wage enhancement.
Education funding: says she has secured more than $1 billion in new state support for public schools in her district.
Housing: describes herself as a leading advocate for affordable housing and landmark housing-reform laws.
Voting access: says she secured additional early-voting and Election Day poll sites for the 2020 general election and the 2021 NYC primary.

positions.summary: Participates in the Assembly's Bipartisan Pro-Choice legislative caucus.
Describes herself as a leading advocate for affordable housing and for landmark housing-reform laws that abolished vacancy decontrol and restricted rent hikes.
Participates in the Assembly's Gun Reform legislative caucus.

record.text: Assembly committee assignments for 2025-2026: Chair of the Aging Committee, plus Codes, Higher Education, Judiciary and Ways and Means.
Was the Assembly's lead sponsor of the state Equal Rights Amendment; voters ratified it as a ballot referendum in the 2024 general election.
Sponsors the "Teach LGBT" curriculum bill directing the state Education Department to develop curriculum on the historical treatment and contributions of LGBT people in America.

Says her bills requiring hate-crime offenders to undergo tolerance training as a sentencing condition, reinstating the Clean Waterways Fund, capping annual lender fees, and requiring health insurance to cover 3-D mammography at no cost, have been signed into law.

candidates.name: Louis Puliafito
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed after Mike Zumbluskas withdrew.

summary.text: Louis Puliafito is the Republican nominee, a longtime Yorkville resident and repeat candidate for this seat (also having run for NY State Senate District 28 in 2024 and Manhattan Borough President in 2021). He worked a 25-year IT career at Merrill Lynch and New York Life, and spent 20 years in SEIU 32BJ residential service, including eight years as a shop steward.

background.text: Earned an associate degree from LaGuardia Community College in 1985.

Built a 25-year career in information technology for Fortune 100 companies, starting in Merrill Lynch's mailroom and later developing financial applications and managing enterprise-wide systems at New York Life Insurance, and supporting charitable initiatives through the New York Life Foundation.
Spent 20 years in SEIU 32BJ residential service, including eight years as a shop steward.
Has run for this Assembly seat multiple times (including 2018 and 2020), for NY State Senate District 28 against Liz Krueger in 2024, and for Manhattan Borough President in 2021, without winning.

priorities.text: Open primaries: says allowing independents to vote in party primaries would broaden the electorate and reduce the influence of party extremes.
Restricting minors' social media use and returning public schools to a renewed focus on paper, pencil and cursive writing alongside reading, writing, math, science and civics.
Affordability and economic opportunity, government accountability and fiscal responsibility, and public safety and quality of life.

positions.summary: Focuses his education platform on curriculum fundamentals (reading, writing, math, science, civics) and limiting technology in classrooms rather than school-choice funding specifically.

sources.title: Assembly Member Rebecca A. Seawright — Biography

researchNotes: No independent campaign website was found for Louis Puliafito; his positions and background come from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response. He has run unsuccessfully for this and other offices several times previously.
